infrastructure: Serbia has above-average internet connectivity for Western Balkans, with Belgrade hosting regional data centres.
Fibre broadband is expanding in urban areas, with significant improvement in recent years.
Serbia's geographic position makes it a transit country for digital connectivity between EU and non-EU Balkans.
talent: Belgrade has a growing tech ecosystem with strong software engineering talent emerging from University of Belgrade.
Serbia has produced notable tech companies (NCR Belgrade, Nordeus) and attracts regional talent.
Brain drain to Germany, Austria, and the UK is significant but partially offset by lower cost of living retaining some talent.
governance: Serbia is a EU accession candidate, with governance reform ongoing but progress slow.
Data protection law broadly aligned with GDPR, though enforcement capacity is developing.
Democratic backsliding concerns have been raised by EU monitors, creating regulatory uncertainty.
investment: Belgrade's tech sector has attracted outsourcing investment from Western companies, creating a services-oriented AI ecosystem.
Serbia has received some EU pre-accession digital transformation funding.
Domestic venture capital is very limited.
economic_readiness: A growing economy with manufacturing, agriculture, and IT services sectors beginning AI integration.
Lower labour costs make Serbia attractive for AI-adjacent services outsourcing.
Limited domestic market size and non-EU status constrain AI product commercialisation.
